title: Cache-Control lacks the {name} directive
description: The response does not carry the {name} directive. Shared and browser caches may keep a copy of a page that contains personal or session data. This check reads the single Cache-Control header and confirms whether no-store is present.
remediation: Send Cache-Control with no-store on responses that carry personal or session data ({safe}).
limitation: Header check on every observed response: a page with no sensitive data fails it, and so does a response with no Cache-Control header at all. The scanner cannot tell which pages are sensitive.
scopeT: Single response header: confirm no-store appears in Cache-Control.
fp: Public static assets that are safe to cache are the common false positive.
recordDesc: A response without {name} can be stored by a cache. Stored copies of sensitive pages can be read by later users of that cache. The remedy is {safe}.
applicability: HTTP responses; the header matters most on authenticated or personal pages.
risk: Sensitive page copies kept in shared or browser caches; LOW severity.
why: The response does not carry the {name} directive.
fix: Set Cache-Control to no-store on authenticated and personal responses.
verifyT: Rescan observes no-store on sensitive responses.

cweDef.name: Use of Cache Containing Sensitive Information
cweDef.summary: Responses with personal or session data that a shared or browser cache keeps can be read by later users of that cache.

title: CORS policy trusts {name}
description: The response sets Access-Control-Allow-Origin to {name}. Sandboxed iframes and some redirects send the null origin, so trusting it lets hostile content read the response.
remediation: Remove null from the CORS allowlist and use {safe}.
limitation: Header value check: it cannot confirm that credentials or sensitive data travel with the response.
scopeT: Single response header value: Access-Control-Allow-Origin equals null.
fp: Responses meant for local tooling that intentionally accepts null are the accepted case.
recordDesc: Trusting the null origin lets sandboxed or redirected content read responses. The remedy is {safe}.
applicability: HTTP responses that send CORS headers.
risk: Cross-origin reads from sandboxed content; MEDIUM severity.
fix: Allowlist only explicit origins, never null.

title: Weak Content-Security-Policy (unsafe-eval)
description: The Content-Security-Policy header allows string-to-code evaluation through the {name} source expression. Injected text can then call eval-style APIs even when inline scripts are blocked.
remediation: Remove unsafe-eval from script-src and move dynamic code to static functions ({safe}).
limitation: Header value check on the token. Policies that also set a nonce for every script still list unsafe-eval, and this check flags them.
scopeT: Single Content-Security-Policy header value: unsafe-eval appears in any directive.
fp: Legacy applications that need eval until a rewrite are the accepted exception.
recordDesc: A policy that keeps {name} lets injected text run through eval-style APIs. The remedy is {safe}.
applicability: HTML responses that send a Content-Security-Policy header.
risk: Reduced XSS protection through eval-style code execution; LOW severity.
verifyT: Rescan shows no unsafe-eval in the policy.

title: Content-Security-Policy without {name}
description: The Content-Security-Policy header does not restrict {name}. This directive has no default-src fallback in CSP, so the restriction must be stated on its own to take effect.
remediation: Add {name} to the policy with a restrictive source list ({safe}).
limitation: Header check: it also fires when no Content-Security-Policy header is sent. DPK-DAST-002 reports that case. The check cannot see a policy delivered by a meta element.
scopeT: Single Content-Security-Policy header value: the named directive is absent.
fp: Pages with no base elements or forms make the gap low-impact; the common false positive.
recordDesc: Without {name} a policy does not restrict that element. Injected markup can use the gap. The remedy is {safe}.
applicability: HTML responses that send a Content-Security-Policy header.
risk: Injected markup redirects relative URLs or form targets; LOW severity.
fix: Add the directive with a restrictive value.

title: Referrer-Policy sends full URLs ({name})
description: The Referrer-Policy header is {name}. Browsers then send the full page URL, including its query string, to every destination, which can carry tokens or identifiers to third parties.
remediation: Use {safe} so cross-origin requests carry only the origin.
limitation: Header value check: it cannot see which URLs carry sensitive query strings.
scopeT: Single Referrer-Policy header value: the unsafe-url token appears.
fp: Pages with no sensitive query strings are the common false positive.
recordDesc: {name} in Referrer-Policy sends full URLs cross-origin. Tokens in query strings can leak. The remedy is {safe}.
applicability: HTML responses that send a Referrer-Policy header.
risk: Query-string tokens or identifiers leaked to third parties; LOW severity.
why: The policy sends the full URL ({name}).
verifyT: Rescan observes a policy that does not send full URLs.

title: Database error text disclosed in a response
description: The response body contains a database driver error ({name}). Driver messages reveal table names, query shape, and engine type, which help an attacker refine injection attempts.
remediation: Catch database errors server-side and return a generic message with a correlation ID ({safe}).
limitation: Marker text on one body: a quoted driver message in documentation or a support article can match.
scopeT: Single response body: confirm no database driver error text is returned.
fp: Pages that quote SQL errors in documentation are the common false positive.
recordDesc: Database driver text in a response exposes query and schema detail. The remedy is {safe}.
applicability: HTTP responses from applications backed by SQL databases.
risk: Schema and query detail that helps injection; MEDIUM severity.
why: The response body carries a database error ({name}).
fix: Return a generic error with a correlation ID.
verifyT: Rescan shows no driver error text in responses.

cells.name: a SQL driver error
cells.safe: a generic error page with a correlation ID

check.valuePattern: You have an error in your SQL syntax|SQLSTATE\[|\bORA-\d{5}|Unclosed quotation mark after the character string|PG::SyntaxError|ERROR:\s+syntax error at or near

observation.body: Error: You have an error in your SQL syntax; check the manual near '' at line 1
SQLSTATE[42000]: Syntax error or access violation
ORA-00933: SQL command not properly ended

title: Node.js stack frame disclosed in a response
description: The response body carries a {name}. Node.js stack frames expose file paths, line numbers, and internal module names to any client that can trigger the error.
remediation: Disable stack output in production and return a generic error page ({safe}).
limitation: Pattern on one body: a Node.js trace quoted in a help article can match. Development output and production exposure look the same.
scopeT: Single response body: confirm no Node.js stack frame with a file, line, and column is returned.
fp: Quoted traces in documentation are the common false positive.
recordDesc: A Node.js stack frame in a response shows server paths and line numbers. The remedy is {safe}.
applicability: HTTP responses from Node.js applications and frameworks.
risk: Server paths and internal layout disclosed to any client; MEDIUM severity.
fix: Return a generic error with a correlation ID.
verifyT: Rescan shows no stack frames in responses.

cells.name: Node.js stack frame
cells.safe: a generic error page with a correlation ID

observation.body: Error handled; see the server log for details.

title: PHP error with a source path disclosed
description: The response body carries a {name}. PHP display_errors prints the message with the file path and line number, which reveals server layout.
remediation: Set display_errors to Off in production and log errors instead ({safe}).
limitation: Pattern on one body: a PHP message quoted in a bug report can match.
scopeT: Single response body: confirm no PHP notice, warning, or fatal error with a file and line is returned.
fp: Quoted messages in documentation are the common false positive.
recordDesc: PHP messages printed to responses include file paths and line numbers. The remedy is {safe}.
risk: Server paths and line numbers disclosed to clients; MEDIUM severity.
why: The response body carries a PHP {name}.
fix: Log errors to a file outside the web root.
verifyT: Rescan shows no PHP messages with paths in responses.

observation.body: Warning: Undefined variable $cart in /var/www/html/shop.php on line 14

title: Server file path disclosed in a response
description: The response body contains a server-side source path ({name}). Absolute paths reveal the deployment layout and framework, which narrows the search for file-based flaws.
remediation: Strip absolute paths from error text and return relative names only ({safe}).
limitation: Pattern on one body: a Windows or Unix path in a download link or log excerpt can match.
scopeT: Single response body: confirm no absolute server path to a source file appears.
fp: Paths that the page displays on purpose, such as a download location, are the common false positive.
recordDesc: An absolute server path in a response reveals the deployment layout. The remedy is {safe}.
applicability: HTTP responses that include error or diagnostic text.
risk: Deployment layout disclosed to clients; LOW severity.
fix: Return relative names in user-visible messages.
verifyT: Rescan shows no absolute source paths in responses.

title: Directory listing enabled
description: The response is an automatic index page ({name}). Anyone can browse file names in that directory, which can expose backups, source, or unlinked files.
remediation: Disable automatic indexes ({safe}) and remove stray backup or source files from the web root.
limitation: Title marker on one body: a page that quotes an index title can match.
scopeT: Single response body: confirm no automatic directory index is returned.
fp: Public download folders that are meant to be browsed are the accepted case.
recordDesc: An automatic index page lists file names in a directory. The remedy is {safe}.
applicability: Web servers that serve directories (Apache and nginx autoindex).
risk: File names and unlinked content exposed to any client; MEDIUM severity.
why: The server returns a {name} for a directory.
fix: Turn autoindex or Options Indexes off.
Remove backup and source files from the web root.
verifyT: Rescan shows no automatic index in responses.

cweDef.name: Exposure of Information Through Directory Listing
cweDef.summary: An automatic index page lists directory contents, which exposes file names, backups, and unlinked resources to any client.

title: Source map reference in a served script
description: The served script ends with {name}. Browsers and attackers can fetch the map and recover original source, comments, and internal paths.
remediation: Do not publish source maps for production bundles, or restrict them to authenticated tooling ({safe}).
limitation: Marker on one body: it only applies to script bodies the scanner captured. It does not prove the map is reachable.
scopeT: Single script body: confirm no sourceMappingURL comment is returned.
fp: Internal builds that publish maps behind access control are the accepted case.
recordDesc: A sourceMappingURL comment points to a map that can restore original source. The remedy is {safe}.
applicability: JavaScript responses from web applications with build pipelines.
risk: Original source and internal comments recovered by anyone; LOW severity.
fix: Remove the sourceMappingURL comment from production bundles.
verifyT: Rescan shows no sourceMappingURL in production scripts.

cells.name: a sourceMappingURL comment
cells.safe: maps kept off the public origin

cweDef.name: Inclusion of Sensitive Information in Source Code
cweDef.summary: Source maps and comments shipped with production scripts let anyone recover original source and internal detail.

title: Debug profiler header exposed
description: The response carries the {name} header. Profiler tooling then exposes request timing, configuration, and internal state to anyone who holds the token.
limitation: Header presence check: the profiler may be protected by a firewall that the scanner cannot see.
scopeT: Single response header: confirm no debug token header is returned.
fp: Development and staging hosts that run the profiler on purpose are the accepted case.
recordDesc: A debug token header links responses to an open profiler. The remedy is {safe}.
applicability: HTTP responses from PHP Symfony and similar frameworks with a profiler.
risk: Internal request and configuration detail reachable through the profiler; MEDIUM severity.
fix: Disable the profiler in production builds.
verifyT: Rescan shows no debug token header on production responses.

cells.name: X-Debug-Token
cells.safe: a production build with the profiler disabled

cweDef.name: Insertion of Sensitive Information Into Debugging Code
cweDef.summary: Debug and profiler tooling left enabled in production exposes request and configuration detail to clients that hold its token.

title: Weak {name} header value
description: The response carries {name}, which lets any host supply script. A wildcard script source lets an injected script run, because the policy does not block it. This check matches the wildcard directly.
limitation: Value check: a host wildcard such as *.example.com is out of scope. It cannot confirm the deployment context.
scopeT: Single response header value: script-src only.
fp: Transitional deployments are the common accepted case.
recordDesc: {name} with a wildcard source lets any host supply script. The policy then stops injected scripts only partly.
risk: Script execution from any host; MEDIUM severity.
